This treatment aims to control prostate cancer and delay progression. The expected benefit depends on your disease setting, previous treatment and general health.
Abiraterone blocks CYP17, an enzyme needed to produce androgens. Prednisolone controls the hormonal effects that can cause low potassium, fluid retention and high blood pressure.

What to watch forNever stop prednisolone suddenly or when abiraterone is held unless the team gives a steroid plan. Ask about a steroid alert card and illness instructions. Contact the team if vomiting prevents you keeping tablets down. Abiraterone with prednisolone must not be combined with radium-223.
Prednisolone suppresses ACTH drive during abiraterone treatment, helping control blood pressure, fluid retention and potassium. It needs its own illness and withdrawal plan.

Bring all prescription, non-prescription and herbal medicines. Check with the oncology pharmacist before starting or stopping anything.

Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) lowers testosterone from the testes. This medicine adds another form of hormone-pathway blockade. Even when cancer becomes castration-resistant, continued testosterone suppression remains part of this treatment unless you have had surgical castration.

Continue your prescribed androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), unless you have had surgery to remove both testes. The team reviews symptoms, blood tests, PSA and scans according to your own plan; there is no universal scan interval. Discuss suitable alternatives, supportive care and the option of declining treatment.

Radiotherapy may treat the prostate, a recurrence or a troublesome site such as a painful bone lesion. Its purpose depends on your disease setting. Ask the team whether it belongs in your plan; starting these tablets does not itself schedule or replace radiotherapy.
Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome.

In COU-AA-302, before chemotherapy for the studied mCRPC population, median overall survival was 34.7 months with abiraterone plus steroid versus 30.3 months with placebo plus steroid. In the post-docetaxel COU-AA-301 final analysis it was 15.8 versus 11.2 months. These are separate trial populations and do not predict your lifespan or the benefit after prior modern ARPI treatment.

previous_short_page.text: What the evidence can tell you Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome. In PROSPER’s high-risk nonmetastatic castration-resistant population, final median overall survival was 67.0 versus 56.3 months with enzalutamide versus placebo, both with ADT (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.61–0.89). In AFFIRM after docetaxel for metastatic disease, the initial median survival was 18.4 versus 13.6 months. ADT lowers testosterone from the testes. Abiraterone blocks CYP17 to reduce androgen production elsewhere too. Prednisolone limits hormonal side effects. This combination can be offered early, before ADT stops controlling the cancer.

Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) lowers testosterone from the testes. This medicine adds another form of hormone-pathway blockade. Even when cancer becomes castration-resistant, continued testosterone suppression remains part of this treatment unless you have had surgical castration.

Research supports a treatment discussion; it cannot predict one person’s outcome.

In the LATITUDE trial’s 2017 analysis of newly diagnosed high-risk metastatic hormone-sensitive cancer, 66% receiving abiraterone plus prednisone and ADT were alive at 3 years versus 49% receiving ADT and placebos (hazard ratio 0.62; 95% confidence interval 0.51–0.76). Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) lowers testosterone from the testes. This medicine adds another form of hormone-pathway blockade. Even when cancer becomes castration-resistant, continued testosterone suppression remains part of this treatment unless you have had surgical castration.
